name: Dark Maroon
lede: Dark Maroon darkens [[maroon]] toward black, a name built by ColorHub's own modifier grammar rather than borrowed from any dictionary, and it shows up almost only as shadow in paintings that carry it.

sections.title: A darkened maroon
sections.body:
Dark Maroon is not an old pigment or dye name: it is the word dark applied to [[maroon]], the brownish red named after the French *marron*, chestnut [1]. The parent color itself was crowdsourced in the xkcd online color survey of 2010, and our naming system darkens its lightness and saturates it slightly to produce this entry [1].

Its nearest neighbor by measured color distance is [[dark-sienna]], about 5.4 units away and a duller version of the same dark red-brown [2]. [[oxblood]] sits a little further off, redder and more vivid, and [[black-bean]] redder still [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color, or something within six units of it, in 74 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.3 per cent, as photographed [3]. Where it appears, it sits in the shadows 77 per cent of the time, almost never as a highlight [3]. The 1500s carry it at roughly three times the archive's overall rate, 21 of 2,231 paintings from that century [3]. As photographed: these are computed color matches on museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not a pigment test [3].

questions.q: Dark Maroon is built by darkening which color?
True or false: in paintings that carry Dark Maroon, it is usually a highlight rather than a shadow.
